newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lower, few to escape down trend.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lower, few to escape down trend.

text.p: Croatian stocks lost ground in sluggish activity on Thursday and traders said few stocks would be able to escape downward trend ahead of a summer season lull.
"I think the prospects for our market are quite discouraging. The level of trading will get weaker as always in summer," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage.
"Everybody is calculating on the summer lull. Prices are pushed down so that money can be made on cheaper stocks in autumn," said Marijana Reskovac of Karlovacka Banka.
"Buyers are definitely not in a hurry now and can wait for a better price," she said.
Seven of 14 active issues fell, two rose, four were flat and one traded for the first time. Volume shrank to 5,092 shares, and turnover was two-thirds down on Wednesday at 2.9 million kuna.
Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara added 11 kuna or 1.86 percent to 601 on volume of 905 shares. It peaked at 610 kuna earlier in the session.
Traders said Karlovacka was poised for further growth.

Karlovacka, a subsidiary of Chile's Compania Cervecerias Unidas, posted excellent results in 1996. It was this week's hot stock on the Zagreb bourse, recording a steady growth from last Friday's close of 500 kuna.
Another gainer, Zagrebacka preference stock, added 10 kuna to 1,480 on volume of 429 shares.
Its ordinary shares edged down 40 kuna to 1,920 with only 232 shares sold while its bearer stock traded flat at 850 kuna, trading 18 shares.
Fully-listed Pliva inched down five kuna to 474, with 21 shares changing hands.
Top decliner electrical group Koncar fell 65 kuna or 5.2 percent to 1,180 kuna, with 31 units sold.
Most actively traded chocolate maker Kras sold 1,038 shares and closed stable at 435 kuna.
Food processor Podravka inched down one kuna to 251 on volume of 588 shares, and traders said it was likely to extend its losses.
Cement factory Nasicecement made its market debut, selling 400 shares at 390 kuna.
